# Sweep Zones domain

## Overview
**Id:** blk-262749aa3aad

Sweep Zones Redux adds a toolbar tool for painting persistent zones. Debris that lands in a sweep zone is marked for sweeping, and moppable puddles in a mop zone get mop errands, at the priority the zone was painted with, until the zone is erased. The mod is `mods/sweep-zones`, static ID `Isochronous.SweepZones`, source in `src/SweepZones/`. It is a from-scratch rewrite of Berkays/Rubacava's Sweep Zones and shares no code or assets with it.

## Key Entities
**Id:** blk-47f9fb177298

### ZoneStore (saved component)
**Id:** blk-d8d071a9cbe4  
**Description**: Holds the painted zones and applies them once a second. Attached to the `SaveGame` object so the zones serialize into the save file (loading without the mod drops them).  
**Location**: `src/SweepZones/ZoneStore.cs`

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| sweepCells | Dictionary<int, PrioritySetting>, saved | Sweep zone cells and the priority each was painted with |
| mopCells | Dictionary<int, PrioritySetting>, saved | Mop zone cells and their priorities |
| Version | int | Bumped on every mutation so the tool's display can cache |
| Instance | ZoneStore | The current store, set in `OnPrefabInit` |

**Relationships**: read and written by `SweepZoneTool`; implements `ISim1000ms`.

### SweepZoneTool
**Id:** blk-8d4b11374898  
**Description**: The box-drag tool, a subclass of the game's `DragTool`. Owns the mode, the zone display (cell colours, perimeter stroke, priority labels) and the toolbar-menu filters. Cursor and area-visualizer assets are cloned from the vanilla Sweep tool by reflection (field names verified against U59-744825).  
**Location**: `src/SweepZones/SweepZoneTool.cs`

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| mode | ZoneMode | `Sweep`, `ClearSweep`, `Mop`, `ClearMop` |
| filters | ToolParameterMenu.ToggleData[] | The four mode toggles in the game's tool side menu (`ModStrings.FilterSweep`, `FilterClearSweep`, `FilterMop`, `FilterClearMop`) |
| cellColors | HashSet<ToolMenu.CellColorData> | Per-cell tint returned by `GetOverlayColorData` |

**Relationships**: uses `ToolMenu.Instance.PriorityScreen` for the painted priority; reads `ZoneStore.Instance`.

### ToolIcon
**Id:** blk-a6045495610f  
**Description**: Registers the toolbar sprite `isochronous_sweepzones_tool` from a PNG embedded in the DLL (resource `SweepZones.assets.tool_icon.png`), with a procedurally drawn fallback. Source art is in `assets-src/`.  
**Location**: `src/SweepZones/ToolIcon.cs`

### Hotkey
**Id:** blk-7d58cc65b189  
**Description**: A PLib `PAction`, `Isochronous.SweepZones.Tool`, default Shift+Z, rebindable under options > game > controls > Mods. Held in `SweepZonesMod.ToolAction`.  
**Location**: `src/SweepZones/Mod.cs`

### Harmony patches
**Id:** blk-8ed739708efc  
**Location**: `src/SweepZones/Patches.cs`

| Target | Kind | Purpose |
|--------|------|---------|
| `Db.Initialize` | Postfix | Registers the tool icon |
| `SaveGame.OnPrefabInit` | Postfix | Adds the `ZoneStore` component |
| `PlayerController.OnPrefabInit` | Postfix | Creates the `SweepZoneTool` object and appends it to `tools` |
| `ToolMenu.CreateBasicTools` | Postfix | Adds the toolbar button, bound to the hotkey action |

## Business Rules
**Id:** blk-a6ab594b39d9

- A zone cell must be an open cell directly above solid ground: not `Grid.Solid`, with a valid solid cell below (`ZoneStore.IsValidZoneCell`). `Grid.Solid` is the sim's material solidity, so surfaces only Duplicants can stand on (open pneumatic doors) are not ground.
- Painting skips invalid cells; erasing is never restricted.
- Each zone cell remembers the priority (including yellow alert) selected when painted.
- Every second, debris in a sweep zone is marked for clearing, unless it is a Duplicant (`GameTags.BaseMinion`, `MinionIdentity`), already marked (`GameTags.Garbage`), or not clearable (critters). A priority already set on an item is never overridden, so manual changes stick.
- Mop zones follow the vanilla mop rules: a liquid cell on a valid zone cell with no placer yet and mass not over the game's `MopTool.maxMopAmt`.
- Each time the tool is activated or its mode switched, `PruneInvalidCells` drops zone cells that no longer qualify (floor dug out, cell built over).
- Erasing a zone keeps errands already created; the vanilla Cancel tool removes them.
- Only the zones of the selected mode's kind are shown (sweep modes show sweep zones, mop modes show mop zones). The display uses the tool's own cell-colouring hook, never an overlay, so overlay-adding mods are unaffected.

## Domain Terminology
**Id:** blk-400a3cb8e2b1

| Term | Definition |
|------|-----------|
| Sweep zone | Painted cells where debris is marked for sweeping |
| Mop zone | Painted cells where moppable puddles get mop errands |
| Region | A 4-connected group of zone cells of one priority; shows one centred priority label |
| Zone cell | A grid cell in `sweepCells` or `mopCells` |

## Key Code Paths
**Id:** blk-a257f96c9ea1

- **Painting**: `DragTool.OnDragTool(cell, ...)` -> `ZoneStore.SetSweep/SetMop/RemoveSweep/RemoveMop` according to `mode`, priority from `PriorityScreen.GetLastSelectedPriority()`. See `src/SweepZones/SweepZoneTool.cs`.
- **Applying zones**: `ZoneStore.Sim1000ms` -> `MarkSweepZones` (walks `Grid.Objects[cell, Pickupables]` and its `objectLayerListItem` chain, `Clearable.MarkForClear`, `Prioritizable.SetMasterPriority`) and `PlaceMopErrands` (instantiates the `MopPlacer` prefab). See `src/SweepZones/ZoneStore.cs`.
- **Display**: `GetOverlayColorData` tints cells; `LateUpdate` -> `RefreshPriorityLabels` rebuilds the outline mesh and region labels (`FindRegions`) whenever `ZoneStore.Version` changes. See `src/SweepZones/SweepZoneTool.cs`.
- **Mode switching**: `OnActivateTool` fills the `ToolParameterMenu`; `OnParametersChanged` sets `mode`; `RefreshModePresentation` prunes, shows or hides the priority screen and sets the hover-card action text.
- **Tool registration**: `PlayerController.OnPrefabInit` patch, then `ToolMenu.CreateBasicTools` patch. See `src/SweepZones/Patches.cs`.
- **Tests**: in-game `[OniTest]` suites in `src/SweepZones.Tests/` (`Zones.cs`, `Marking.cs`, `Painting.cs`, `Display.cs`, `ByHand.cs`).

## Related
**Id:** blk-7c53bf2eeb5b

- See also: [glossary](glossary.md)

# Sweep Zones glossary

Terms for the Sweep Zones Redux mod. For the mod's entities, rules and code paths see [entities](entities.md).

## Abbreviations and Acronyms
**Id:** blk-5ae33d3b4365

| Abbreviation | Full Term | Context |
|--------------|-----------|---------|
| ONI | Oxygen Not Included | The game the mod is for |
| U59 | Game update 59 | The build line the rewrite targets (`minimumSupportedBuild` 744825) |
| PLib | Peter Han's mod library | Hotkey action; merged into the DLL |
| DLC | Downloadable content | The mod supports all of them (`supportedContent: ALL`) |

## Terms to Avoid
**Id:** blk-090e762eefa7

| Avoid | Use Instead | Reason |
|-------|-------------|--------|
| Overlay (for the zone display) | Zone display | The mod deliberately adds no overlay; the display is the tool's own cell colouring |
| Sweep Zones (the original) | Berkays/Rubacava's Sweep Zones | This mod is Sweep Zones Redux; no code or assets are shared with the original |
| Erase (for cancelling errands) | Cancel | Erasing a zone leaves existing errands; the vanilla Cancel tool removes them |

## Cross-Domain Terms
**Id:** blk-5208ff35a917

### Sweep
**Id:** blk-144b7d3367fc  
**Definition**: The game's errand that has a Duplicant pick up loose debris and put it in storage. `Clearable.MarkForClear` creates it and adds `GameTags.Garbage`.  
**Used in**: `ZoneStore.MarkSweepZones`.

### Mop
**Id:** blk-d6420be85bee  
**Definition**: The game's errand that removes a thin liquid layer (150 kg or less) from a floor cell, made by a `MopPlacer` object.  
**Used in**: `ZoneStore.PlaceMopErrands`.

### Debris
**Id:** blk-f7a50b55fa0c  
**Definition**: Loose items on the ground, the `Pickupable` objects on the `Pickupables` object layer.  
**Used in**: `ZoneStore.MarkSweepZones`.

### PrioritySetting
**Id:** blk-4b9fe829e6b8  
**Definition**: The game's priority value (a class and a number from 1 to 9, with yellow alert above). Zones store one per cell and apply it with `Prioritizable.SetMasterPriority`.  
**Used in**: `ZoneStore.cs`, `SweepZoneTool.cs`.

### DragTool
**Id:** blk-cc60e721fd5b  
**Definition**: The game's base class for box-drag tools. `SweepZoneTool` subclasses it and implements `OnDragTool` per cell.  
**Used in**: `SweepZoneTool.cs`.

### ToolParameterMenu
**Id:** blk-4734bb46c709  
**Definition**: The game's side menu of toggle options for the active tool. It holds the four mode toggles.  
**Used in**: `SweepZoneTool.OnActivateTool`.

### Cell
**Id:** blk-c1edf9b20db2  
**Definition**: One tile of the world grid, addressed by an int index; saved zones are keyed by it.  
**Used in**: `ZoneStore.cs`.

## Related
**Id:** blk-3d3e2c8c1cc5

- See also: [entities](entities.md)

# sweep-zones

## What this is
**Id:** blk-5cf836ddb339

Sweep Zones Redux is an Oxygen Not Included mod that adds a Sweep Zones tool to the toolbar. Players paint persistent zones, and debris that lands in a sweep zone is marked for sweeping, and moppable puddles in a mop zone get mop errands, at the priority the zone was painted with, until the zone is erased. The tool has four box-drag modes (sweep zone, erase sweep zone, mop zone, erase mop zone), remembers priority per cell including yellow alert, and shows priority labels over each contiguous same-priority region. It is a ground-up rewrite of the feature set of Berkays/Rubacava's Sweep Zones and shares no code or assets with it. Version 1.6.0. Targets the current game (U59+) with all DLC content (minimumSupportedBuild 744825).

## Where things are
**Id:** blk-7ba496c215ac

- `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: player-facing description and release notes.
- `src/SweepZones/`: the mod. `Mod.cs` (entry point), `SweepZoneTool.cs` (the paint tool), `ZoneStore.cs` (the saved zone store), `ToolIcon.cs` (toolbar icons), `Patches.cs` (Harmony patches), `ModStrings.cs` (UI strings), `mod.yaml` and `mod_info.yaml` (manifests).
- `src/SweepZones/assets/`: `tool_icon.png`.
- `src/SweepZones/translations/`: `.pot` template and `ko`, `ru`, `zh` po files.
- `src/SweepZones.Tests/`: in-game tests (zones, painting, marking, display, by-hand play).
- `assets-src/IconGen/`: the program that generates the tool icons; `assets-src/captures/`: reference captures of the icons and zones.
- `publish/`: Workshop description, preview image, workshop id and the old obsolete-mod description.
- `.context/`: `overview.md`, `domains/` ([entities](domains/entities.md), [glossary](domains/glossary.md)), `standards/` ([code-style](standards/code-style.md), [error-handling](standards/error-handling.md), [naming-conventions](standards/naming-conventions.md)), `decisions/`, `retrospectives/`, `META.md`, `projects.md`.

---
doc_id: doc-b35b5c30a8f8
description: "C# code style for the Sweep Zones Redux mod: formatting, imports, comments, Harmony patch and game component conventions, plus a section on its hotkey action, zone store component and drag tool"
applies_to:
  - "src/**"
---

# Code Style Guide

## Formatting
**Id:** blk-42df3a59da99

### Indentation
**Id:** blk-1d9ad5f30869

- Tabs, one per level, in every `.cs` file (`mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Mod.cs`).
- Project files (`.csproj`, `common/oni-mod.props`, `common/oni-mod.targets`) use two spaces.
- Files are committed with LF line endings; Windows checkouts convert them to CRLF (`core.autocrlf` is true), so do not hand-normalise line endings.

### Line Length
**Id:** blk-c02be4756c7c

- No limit is configured and the repository has no `.editorconfig`.
- Wrap long calls and string concatenations after an argument or before a `+`, and indent the continuation one tab. The start-up log call in `mods/jumper-bridges/src/JumperBridges/Mod.cs` is the pattern.
- TODO(owner): decide whether to add an `.editorconfig` recording tabs and brace placement so editors enforce what the code already does.

### Braces
**Id:** blk-064a58168248

- Opening brace on its own line (Allman) for namespaces, types, members and multi-line control blocks.
- A body of one short statement goes on the next line without braces:

```csharp
foreach (Mod mod in mods)
{
	if (!mod.IsEnabledForActiveDlc())
		continue;
	...
}
```

- Multi-line initialisers and enums end with a trailing comma (`YieldToWorkshopIds` in `mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Mod.cs`, `CoolPodMode` in `mods/storage-pod-redux/src/StoragePodRedux/Options.cs`).

## Language and Toolchain
**Id:** blk-2f4e844db89e

- C# 9 on .NET Framework 4.8 (`LangVersion` 9.0 and `TargetFramework` net48 in `common/oni-mod.props`). Namespace blocks, not file-scoped namespaces; no nullable reference types.
- Mods compile against the game's own assemblies (`common/oni-mod.targets`): `Assembly-CSharp`, `Assembly-CSharp-firstpass`, `0Harmony` and Unity modules. The game's .NET Framework lacks some newer APIs (`ConditionalWeakTable.AddOrUpdate` is missing, see `mods/detect-any-element/src/DetectAnyElement/Patches.cs`).
- Optional references are switched on in the mod csproj before the targets import: `ReferenceUnityUI`, `ReferenceImageConversion`, `UsePLib` (PLib is ILRepack-merged into the mod DLL) and `UseTranslations` (compiles `common/src/Translations.cs` in).
- One namespace per mod, equal to its `RootNamespace`. Subfolders organise files and do not add namespaces (`mods/upgrade-planner/src/UpgradePlanner/Plan`, `Rules`, `Tool`, `UI` all declare `namespace UpgradePlanner`).

## Imports/Includes
**Id:** blk-faa925a5196c

### Organization
**Id:** blk-c912752fe0ac

`using` directives sit above the namespace, in one block with no blank lines, sorted alphabetically with `System.*` first. Aliases for `ModStrings` branches come last.

1. `System.*`
2. Everything else alphabetically: `HarmonyLib`, `Isochronous`, `KMod`, `Newtonsoft.Json`, `PeterHan.PLib.*`, `ProcGenGame`, `UnityEngine`
3. Aliases (`using TOOL = SweepZones.ModStrings.UI.TOOLS.SWEEPZONES;`)

### Example
**Id:** blk-8ce83687722f

```csharp
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Reflection;
using HarmonyLib;
using Isochronous;
using Klei;
using KMod;
using STRINGS;
using UnityEngine;
```
(`mods/salty-surf/src/SaltySurf/Mod.cs`)

`Debug.Log` resolves either to `UnityEngine.Debug` or to the game's own global `Debug` class, so several `Mod.cs` files omit `using UnityEngine`. When a file imports `System.Diagnostics`, qualify the call as `UnityEngine.Debug.Log` (`mods/just-fall-already/src/JustFallAlready/FallPoke.cs`).

## Comments
**Id:** blk-698de825a898

### When to Comment
**Id:** blk-6090624fb2d7

- On every non-trivial class, an XML `<summary>` that says what the game does and what the patch changes, so a reader can check the patch against the game code. The long summary on `OvercrowdingMonitor_UpdateRegion_Patch` in `mods/dont-count-eggs-on-rails/src/DontCountEggsOnRails/Mod.cs` is the model.
- Where a game quirk forces an odd line: `// The game's .NET Framework has no AddOrUpdate on this table.`
- Where another mod is involved, name it and its Workshop id (`mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Mod.cs`, `mods/smart-weight-plate/src/SmartWeightPlate/Mod.cs`).
- Escape angle brackets in XML comments as `<` and `>`.

### When NOT to Comment
**Id:** blk-12ba1a8af609

- Code that reads clearly from its names.
- Commented-out code; delete it.
- Restating what a line does.

### Format
**Id:** blk-83105206af84

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// The "Any" choice. It is a tag like the elements a sensor's Filterable holds, so it rides
/// in the same saved field and copies with the building's settings.
/// </summary>
public static class AnyElement

// Single-line note for a quirk or a reason.
```

## Control Structures
**Id:** blk-32740201df97

### Conditionals
**Id:** blk-b81f5e0f86a9

Guard clauses and early `return` or `continue` keep nesting shallow (`SettleSimBackwalls.UpdateFromSim` in `mods/natural-backwalls-everywhere/src/NaturalBackwalls/SettleSimPatch.cs`):

```csharp
if (!Grid.IsValidCell(cell))
	continue;
ushort idx = data->backwallElement[cell];
if (idx == ushort.MaxValue || idx >= elements.Count)
	continue;
```

### Loops
**Id:** blk-6958eb513dec

- Plain `for` and `foreach`. Code that runs every sim tick or frame avoids LINQ and allocations; reuse scratch lists (`scratch` in `mods/just-fall-already/src/JustFallAlready/FallPoke.cs`).
- Local types are written out (`Tech tech = ...`). `var` appears mainly in `mods/upgrade-planner`, `mods/natural-backwalls-everywhere` and the test projects; follow the surrounding file.

### Strings
**Id:** blk-417ad5f3c6ec

- Log and UI text is built with `+` concatenation, or `string.Format` on a `LocString`. String interpolation is not used in mod code.
- Player-visible text is a `LocString` field in `ModStrings`, never a literal at the call site (see [naming conventions](naming-conventions.md)).

## Harmony Patches
**Id:** blk-e0fdf1ca5ef2

- A patch is a static class with `[HarmonyPatch(typeof(Type), nameof(Type.Method))]`, or `[HarmonyPatch(typeof(Type), "PrivateMethod")]` for a non-public method, and methods named `Prefix`, `Postfix`, `Transpiler` or `Finalizer` (`mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Patches.cs`).
- Game state arrives through Harmony parameters: `__instance`, `__result`, `___field`. Fields read repeatedly use `AccessTools.FieldRefAccess` kept in a `static readonly` field (`mods/detect-any-element/src/DetectAnyElement/Patches.cs`).
- A prefix returns `true` to let the game's method run and `false` only when it replaces the method (`mods/dont-count-eggs-on-rails`, `mods/bitshifter` `UpdateVisuals`).
- A patch that depends on an option implements `Prepare()` (`mods/jumper-bridges/src/JumperBridges/Patches.cs`); a patch with several targets implements `TargetMethods()`.
- `UserMod2.OnLoad` calls `base.OnLoad(harmony)`, which applies every patch in the assembly, then registers libraries and logs the version. A mod that must patch after all others applies its patches from `OnAllModsLoaded` instead (`mods/bitshifter/src/Bitshifter/Mod.cs`).
- Transpilers search for the instruction they change and report when it is not found; see [error handling](error-handling.md).

## Game Components
**Id:** blk-c603763d457b

- A component extends `KMonoBehaviour`, overrides `OnPrefabInit`, `OnSpawn` and `OnCleanUp` and calls `base` from each. Sibling components come in through `[MyCmpGet]` or `[MyCmpReq]` (`mods/no-magic-fridges/src/NoMagicFridges/FridgeThermostat.cs`).
- Saved state uses `[Serialize]` fields with `[SerializationConfig(MemberSerialization.OptIn)]` on the class (`mods/sweep-zones/src/SweepZones/ZoneStore.cs`).
- Components are added to prefabs from a `DoPostConfigureComplete` postfix with `go.AddOrGet<T>()`.

## Project-Specific Rules
**Id:** blk-9543e106622d

- Mod options are a PLib `POptions` class marked `[JsonObject(MemberSerialization.OptIn)]` and `[ConfigFile(SharedConfigLocation: true)]`, read through a static `Load()` (`mods/vent-freeze-fix/src/VentFreezeFix/Options.cs`) or through `SingletonOptions<Options>` (`mods/storage-pod-redux`). Option titles are string-table keys, so the translation follows the language.
- Every mod logs one line at load: `[<Name>] Loaded version <assembly version>`.
- Tests live in a separate `<Name>.Tests` project and are written as `[OniTest]` coroutines against the real game.

### Sweep Zones Redux specifics
**Id:** blk-e3db311484c0

- `UsePLib`, `UseTranslations` and `ReferenceUnityUI`. The rebindable hotkey is a PLib action created in `OnLoad`; `SweepZonesMod.ToolAction` holds `PAction.MaxAction` until then (`src/SweepZones/Mod.cs`).
- `ZoneStore` is a `KMonoBehaviour, ISim1000ms` with `[SerializationConfig(MemberSerialization.OptIn)]` and `[Serialize]` dictionaries; it is attached to the `SaveGame` object so the zones save with the game. The static `Instance` is set in `OnPrefabInit` and cleared in `OnCleanUp` only when `Instance == this`.
- `SweepZoneTool` is a `DragTool` that copies cursor and visualizer fields from a donor tool by reflection (`CopyField`).
- `using TOOL = SweepZones.ModStrings.UI.TOOLS.SWEEPZONES;` aliases the string branch.

## Related
**Id:** blk-37783b691bda

- See also: [naming conventions](naming-conventions.md)
- See also: [error handling](error-handling.md)
